subject: FY27 Preliminary Budget Recommendations
overview: The Medford School Committee received a presentation on preliminary FY27 budget recommendations totaling $94 million, reviewed student survey results regarding high school lunch and busing conditions, and received an update on the MSBA high school building project.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee voted to enter executive session to discuss strategy regarding non-union personnel contract negotiations.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: Approved routine consent items including bills and payroll, budget transfers, donations, field trips, and meeting minutes from March 16, 2026.

items.title: Mustang Moments
items.summary: The committee recognized student achievement through presentations by the Missittuck School Council, the MHS Unified Physical Education program, and poster contest winner Nora Shaw.

items.title: Introduction of Transportation Manager
items.summary: Superintendent Galusi formally introduced Ina J. Williams as the district's new transportation manager.

items.title: FY27 Preliminary Budget Recommendations
items.summary: District finance staff presented a preliminary FY27 budget request of $94,032,696, detailing fixed cost increases, special education needs, and departmental investment priorities.

items.title: Approval of Prior Year Invoices: Gone Green Billing
items.summary: Approved the payment of $48,665.51 for unprocessed fiscal year 2025 electrical vendor invoices.

items.title: Student Advisory Council Survey Report
items.summary: Student representatives presented survey findings highlighting student concerns regarding cafeteria line crowding, limited meal time, and bus transportation logistics.

items.title: MSBA High School Building Project Update
items.summary: Member Graham reported on the submission of six site design options to the MSBA and outlined next steps for space evaluation and community outreach.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: The committee expressed condolences to the families of former teacher and coach David P. Skerry and former security monitor Lot Max Parajan.
